summary: Per Dr. Pham's rulings, inositol receives at most low credit for limited cycle-regularity findings in women with PCOS: 36703143's primary outcome pooled 2 trials (118 women; RR 1.79, 1.13-2.85; very low certainty), and neither trial is one of the review's retracted reports. The guideline review 38163998 (limited, inconclusive) carries no credit. Fertility, pregnancy, live-birth, ovulation, ovarian and hormone-balance claims are excluded, and the record-level hold is lifted with a notes citation.

references_structured.title: Inositol is an effective and safe treatment in polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
supports_claims: Cycle regularity and selected metabolic or hormonal outcomes in PCOS
references_structured.notes: The retained positive review includes primary studies now carrying retractions or expressions of concern. Its affirmative cycle/metabolic aggregate is not revalidated by this batch; retain the paper as history and do not use its unqualified pooled conclusion as affirmative credit until a scoped analysis supports it. Underlying primary notices: PMID 18074942 -> PMID 37782148; PMID 20222840 -> PMID 42304764; PMID 28485095 -> PMID 36848124; PMID 28980870 -> PMID 33143512, PMID 38758364. Keep the separate limited/inconclusive38163998 and null/mixed35477841 source conclusions; do not infer every inositol outcome is ineffective. 2026-10-28 scoped analysis (agent review, Dr. Pham ruling of 2026-10-28): the only credited outcome, menstrual-cycle regularity (as reported) versus control, pools Pourghasem 2018 and Donne 2019 (Figure 2); neither is a flagged report (18074942, 20222840, 28485095, 28980870). Other pooled outcomes of this review remain uncredited.

references_structured.title: Efficacy of Myo-inositol on Anthropometric, Metabolic, and Endocrine Outcomes in PCOS Patients: a Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trial.
supports_claims: No clinically significant improvement across most anthropometric, metabolic, and endocrine outcomes; high heterogeneity

applicability.studied_population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome; limited, very-low-certainty cycle-regularity findings only; not fertility, ovulation, pregnancy, live birth, ovarian or hormone-balance outcomes.

record_updates.notes: Human evidence is condition-specific and conflicting. A 2023 review reported improvement in cycle regularity and selected metabolic outcomes, while a 2022 meta-analysis found no clinically significant improvement across most anthropometric, metabolic, and endocrine outcomes. The systematic review used for the 2023 international PCOS guideline update concluded that evidence was limited and inconclusive. This record is not broad proof for weight loss, fertility, or glucose control outside PCOS. Live included-study inspection of38163998 identifies retracted primary26507336/18462730;36703143 includes retracted18074942/28980870 (and prior related integrity notices). The parent reviews themselves are not declared retracted. No independently accepted current product/outcome scope is supplied by this source-extraction batch. Retain separate limited/inconclusive38163998 and null/mixed35477841 findings; withhold the unresolved affirmative relationship without inventing a recomputed pooled result, efficacy-negative judgment, dose penalty or safety warning. Dr. Pham's signed ruling of 2026-10-28 resolves the former record-level eligibility hold: at most low credit for limited cycle-regularity findings in women with PCOS only; no fertility, ovulation, ovarian or hormone-balance claim. The credited pool (Pourghasem 2018, Donne 2019; Figure 2 of 36703143) contains neither flagged retracted report.

identity.preparation: Myo-inositol and inositol combinations (Figure 2 'combined inositols' subgroup; Table 1 lists MI 4000 mg/day for both pooled trials); not a preferred form

population.description: Women with PCOS; overall 26 RCTs and 1691 patients; the placebo cycle-regularity pool is 2 trials (Pourghasem 2018, Iran; Donne 2019, Italy) with 118 women, mostly in their 30s with mean BMI <30.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing inositols with placebo or metformin; primary outcome changed (protocol deviation stated) to menstrual-cycle normalization.

outcomes.name: Primary: limited cycle-regularity findings versus placebo/control, RR 1.79 (95% CI 1.13-2.85), 2 trials, 118 women, I2 0%, GRADE very low (the source labels this outcome 'cycle normalization')
Versus metformin: cycle regularity RR 1.42 (0.8-2.53), not significant; this is not proof of non-inferiority
Secondary versus placebo: BMI MD -0.45, fasting glucose MD -3.14 mg/dl, total testosterone MD -20.39 ng/dl, SHBG higher

limitations: Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling: at most limited, narrow PCOS credit for cycle regularity; no hormone-balance, ovarian or fertility claim; no preferred form or dose.
The credited estimate rests on 2 small trials (118 women) with very low certainty; Donne 2019's comparator is listed as diet in Table 1, and cycle-regularity definitions varied (Discussion).

Neither pooled cycle trial is among the retracted included reports (18074942, 28980870), which feed other outcomes of this review; those retractions remain flagged and other outcomes are not credited.
The guideline-informing review 38163998 judges inositol evidence for PCOS limited and inconclusive overall; this credit is confined to cycle regularity.
